solve.work: Cutting off a corner between two adjacent midpoints: a triangle and a 5-sided piece.

questions.stem: A square is cut along both of its corner-to-corner lines into 4 triangles. Then each triangle is cut in half by one straight line from its square corner to the middle of its longest side. How many pieces are there in all?
questions.solution: The first cuts make 4 triangles. Cutting each of them in half makes 4 x 2 = 8 pieces.

questions.stem: A big square is made of 3 rows of 3 small squares. Ray cuts off 1 whole row of 3 small squares. How many small squares are left?
questions.solution: 3 rows of 3 is 9 small squares. Taking away one row of 3 leaves 9 - 3 = 6.

questions.stem: Which statement is true?
choices: A circle can be cut into 2 triangles with 1 straight cut.
A square can be cut into 2 triangles with 1 straight cut.
A triangle can be cut into 2 squares with 1 straight cut.
A square can be cut into 3 triangles with 1 straight cut.
questions.answer: A square can be cut into 2 triangles with 1 straight cut.
questions.solution: One cut from corner to opposite corner turns a square into 2 triangles. One cut always makes 2 pieces, a circle has no corners, and a triangle cannot be cut into squares.

solve.answer: A square can be cut into 2 triangles with 1 straight cut.
solve.work: A diagonal cuts a square into 2 triangles.

questions.stem: A rectangle that is not a square is folded along a line from one corner to the opposite corner. Is this fold a line of symmetry?
choices: Yes, because both halves are triangles of the same size, so they must match.
Yes, because the line goes from one corner to the opposite corner and cuts the rectangle in half.
No, because the corners do not land on each other, so the halves do not match.
No, because a rectangle that is not a square has no lines of symmetry at all.
questions.answer: No, because the corners do not land on each other, so the halves do not match.
questions.solution: When the rectangle is folded along a corner-to-corner line, the long side and the short side do not land on each other. The halves do not match, so it is not a line of symmetry. (A rectangle does have 2 other lines of symmetry.)

solve.answer: No, because the corners do not land on each other, so the halves do not match.
solve.work: Diagonal of a non-square rectangle splits it into 2 congruent triangles, but folding does not make them land on each other (reflection over the diagonal does not map the rectangle to itself). A rectangle has 2 lines of symmetry, so option B is false.

questions.stem: A line of symmetry is a fold line that makes the two halves of a shape match exactly. A square has 4 lines of symmetry and a rectangle that is not a square has 2 lines of symmetry. How many lines of symmetry do the two shapes have in all?
questions.solution: 4 + 2 = 6 lines of symmetry.

questions.stem: Which shape has exactly 3 lines of symmetry (3 different fold lines that make the two halves match)?
choices: a triangle with exactly 2 sides the same length
a rectangle that is not a square
a triangle with all 3 sides the same length
questions.answer: a triangle with all 3 sides the same length
questions.solution: A triangle with 3 equal sides has 3 lines of symmetry. The triangle with 2 equal sides has 1, the rectangle has 2 and the square has 4.

solve.answer: a triangle with all 3 sides the same length
solve.work: Equilateral triangle has 3 lines of symmetry.

questions.solution: The middle splits the meter stick into 2 equal parts. Half of 100 centimeters is 50 centimeters.

solve.work: Middle of 100 cm is 50 cm from the 0 end.

questions.skill: Measure length with a ruler or tape
questions.stem: A leaf is lined up with a ruler. One end of the leaf is at the 3 inch mark. The other end is at the 11 inch mark. How long is the leaf, in inches?
questions.solution: The leaf does not start at 0, so subtract the two marks: $11 - 3 = 8$ inches. You can also count the inches from 3 up to 11: that is 8.

questions.skill: Measure length with a ruler or tape
questions.stem: A pen is lined up with a ruler. One end of the pen is at the 0 mark. The other end is just past the 15 centimeter mark and is much closer to 15 than to 16. To the nearest centimeter, how long is the pen, in centimeters?
questions.solution: The end of the pen is closest to the 15 centimeter mark, and the pen starts at 0. To the nearest centimeter, the pen is 15 centimeters long.

solve.work: Just past 15 and much closer to 15 than 16, so 15 cm to the nearest cm.

questions.stem: Ben measures the length of a soccer field and then the length of a house key. Which pair of units fits best, in that order?
questions.solution: A soccer field is very long, so use the bigger unit, meters. A key is very short, so use the smaller unit, centimeters.

solve.work: A soccer field is about 100 m (meters); a house key is about 5 cm (centimeters).

questions.stem: Which is the best estimate for the height of a classroom door?
questions.solution: A door is a bit taller than a grown-up, about 7 feet. 7 inches is only as long as a pencil. 7 yards or 7 meters would be as tall as a house.

solve.work: A door is about 7 feet tall (about 2 m). 7 m, 7 yd (21 ft) and 7 in are all wrong.

questions.stem: Ana guesses that her desk is 60 centimeters wide. Then she measures it and finds that it is 64 centimeters wide. How many centimeters off was her guess?
questions.solution: Find the difference between the guess and the measurement: $64 - 60 = 4$ centimeters.

questions.stem: Sam measures a desk with his pencil and counts 6 pencil lengths. Tia measures the same desk with a paper clip and counts 15 paper clip lengths. Which is longer, one pencil or one paper clip?
questions.solution: It is the same desk. The shorter unit needs more copies to cover it. It takes fewer pencils than paper clips, so the pencil is the longer unit.

solve.work: Same desk: fewer pencils (6) than paper clips (15) are needed, so the pencil is the longer unit.

questions.stem: Jo measures a rug with a meter stick and finds that it is 3 meters long. One meter is 100 centimeters. How long is the rug, in centimeters?
questions.solution: Count by hundreds, once for each meter: 100, 200, 300. The rug is 300 centimeters long.

questions.skill: Compare lengths and find the difference
questions.stem: A rope is 83 centimeters long. A ribbon is 49 centimeters long. How many centimeters longer is the rope than the ribbon?
questions.solution: Subtract the shorter length from the longer one: $83 - 49 = 34$ centimeters. Check: $49 + 34 = 83$.

questions.skill: Compare lengths and find the difference
questions.stem: Which list puts these lengths in order from shortest to longest: 28 centimeters, 82 centimeters, 8 centimeters, 48 centimeters?
questions.solution: Compare the numbers: 8 is the least, then 28, then 48, then 82. The shortest comes first.

questions.stem: A rope is 45 inches long. Dee cuts off a piece that is 18 inches long. How many inches long is the rest of the rope?
questions.solution: Subtract the piece that was cut off: $45 - 18 = 27$ inches. Check: $27 + 18 = 45$.

questions.skill: Measure length with a ruler or tape
questions.stem: A pencil is lined up with a ruler. One end is at the 2 inch mark and the other end is at the 9 inch mark. How long is the pencil, in inches?
questions.solution: The pencil does not start at 0. Subtract: 9 - 2 = 7 inches.

questions.skill: Measure length with a ruler or tape
questions.stem: A key is lined up with a ruler. One end is at the 0 mark. The other end is just past the 6 centimeter mark, and much closer to 6 than to 7. To the nearest centimeter, how long is the key?
questions.solution: The end is much closer to 6 than to 7, so the key is about 6 centimeters long.

solve.work: Just past 6, much closer to 6: rounds to 6 cm.

questions.skill: Measure length with a ruler or tape
questions.stem: A cord is laid along a measuring tape in centimeters. One end is at the 25 mark and the other end is at the 40 mark. How long is the cord, in centimeters?
questions.solution: The cord does not start at 0. Subtract: 40 - 25 = 15.

questions.skill: Measure length with a ruler or tape
questions.stem: Lena says that a stick from the 4 inch mark to the 10 inch mark is 10 inches long. What did she do wrong?
choices: She forgot that the stick starts at 4, not at 0
questions.answer: She forgot that the stick starts at 4, not at 0
questions.solution: The length is 10 - 4 = 6 inches. Lena read only the end mark.

solve.answer: She forgot that the stick starts at 4, not at 0

questions.stem: Ravi covers a shelf with blocks end to end, with no gaps and no overlap. He uses 7 blocks, and each block is 3 inches long. How long is the shelf, in inches?
questions.solution: 7 blocks of 3 inches: 7 x 3 = 21.

questions.stem: A hallway is 24 feet long. Jo wants to cover it with mats end to end. Each mat is 4 feet long. How many mats does she need?
questions.solution: 4 + 4 + 4 + 4 + 4 + 4 = 24, so she needs 6 mats.

questions.stem: Ben measures the length of a playground and then the length of a bean. Which units fit best, in that order?
questions.solution: A playground is long, so use meters. A bean is tiny, so use centimeters.

solve.work: Playground in meters, bean in centimeters.

questions.stem: Mia measures the height of a door and the length of a crayon. Which units fit best, in that order?
questions.solution: A door is tall, so feet fit. A crayon is short, so inches fit.

solve.work: Door height in feet, crayon in inches.

questions.stem: Which is the best unit for telling how long a school bus is?
questions.solution: A bus is long but not miles long. Meters fit best.

questions.stem: Kim measures a table with her hand and counts 8 hands. Lee measures the same table with a ruler marked in inches and counts 24 inches. Which is longer, 1 hand or 1 inch?
questions.solution: The table is the same. It took fewer hands than inches, so a hand is longer.

solve.work: Same table: 8 hands = 24 inches, so fewer, longer units: a hand is longer.

questions.stem: A shelf is 2 meters long. One meter is 100 centimeters. How long is the shelf, in centimeters?
Joe measures a rope in feet and gets 6. Ann measures the same rope in yards and gets 2. Why is Joe's number bigger?
choices: A foot is longer than a yard
A yard is shorter than a foot
A foot is shorter than a yard, so it takes more feet
questions.answer: A foot is shorter than a yard, so it takes more feet
questions.solution: A foot is shorter than a yard. It takes more of the shorter unit to cover the same rope.

solve.answer: A foot is shorter than a yard, so it takes more feet
solve.work: Shorter unit, more units: 6 feet = 2 yards.

questions.stem: Dee measures a hall with her steps. One step is half of a meter. She takes 10 steps. How many meters long is the hall?
questions.solution: 10 steps of half a meter: 5 meters.

questions.stem: Which is the best estimate for the height of a kitchen table?
questions.solution: A table comes up to about a child's waist, about 3 feet.

solve.work: A table is about 2.5-3 ft high.

questions.stem: Ola guesses that a rug is 150 centimeters long. She measures it and finds that it is 162 centimeters long. How many centimeters off was her guess?
Which is the best estimate for the length of a soccer field?
questions.solution: A soccer field is long, about 100 meters. 100 centimeters is only about one big step.

solve.work: A soccer field is about 100 m long.

questions.skill: Compare lengths and find the difference
questions.stem: A rope is 92 centimeters long. A ribbon is 57 centimeters long. How many centimeters longer is the rope than the ribbon?

questions.skill: Compare lengths and find the difference
questions.stem: Which list puts these lengths in order from longest to shortest: 35 inches, 53 inches, 5 inches, 43 inches?
questions.solution: Compare tens first: 53, 43, 35, then 5.

questions.skill: Compare lengths and find the difference
questions.stem: Pam jumps 48 inches. Quin jumps 36 inches. Ray jumps 40 inches. How many inches longer is the longest jump than the shortest jump?
questions.solution: The longest is 48 and the shortest is 36. 48 - 36 = 12.

questions.stem: A fence has 5 boards in a row end to end. Each board is 2 meters long. How long is the fence, in meters?
questions.solution: 5 boards of 2 meters: 2 + 2 + 2 + 2 + 2 = 10.

questions.stem: An inch is longer than a centimeter. Ben measures a book in inches and gets 8. Cara measures the same book in centimeters. Which is true about Cara's number?
choices: It is less than 8, because centimeters are shorter
It is exactly 8, because the book has only one length
It is less than 8, because centimeters are longer
It is more than 8, because centimeters are shorter
questions.answer: It is more than 8, because centimeters are shorter
questions.solution: A centimeter is a shorter unit than an inch, so it takes more centimeters to cover the same book. Cara's number is more than 8.

solve.answer: It is more than 8, because centimeters are shorter
solve.work: Smaller unit gives a larger number: more than 8 because centimeters are shorter (about 20 cm).

questions.stem: One yard is 3 feet. Eli's board is 2 yards long. Fay's board is 5 feet long. Whose board is longer?
choices: Eli's board, because 2 yards is 6 feet
Fay's board, because 5 is more than 2
Neither, they are the same length
Fay's board, because feet are longer than yards
questions.answer: Eli's board, because 2 yards is 6 feet
questions.solution: Put both lengths in feet. 2 yards is $2 \times 3 = 6$ feet. Fay's board is 5 feet. 6 feet is more than 5 feet, so Eli's board is longer.

solve.answer: Eli's board, because 2 yards is 6 feet
solve.work: 2 yards = 6 feet > 5 feet, so Eli's board.

questions.skill: Measure with a ruler or meter stick
questions.stem: Ana wants to cut a ribbon that is 18 centimeters long. She lines up one end of the ribbon at the 7 centimeter mark on a ruler. At which centimeter mark should the other end of the ribbon be?
questions.solution: The ribbon starts at the 7 mark and is 18 centimeters long, so it ends 18 marks farther along. $7 + 18 = 25$.

solve.work: Start at 7, length 18: 7+18 = 25. (The other direction would be negative, so 25 is the only answer.)

questions.skill: Measure length with a ruler or tape
questions.stem: A ribbon is laid along a measuring tape. One end of the ribbon is at the 14 centimeter mark. The other end is at the 37 centimeter mark. How long is the ribbon, in centimeters?
questions.solution: The ribbon does not start at 0, so subtract the two marks: $37 - 14 = 23$ centimeters.

questions.skill: Measure length with a ruler or tape
questions.stem: On a ruler, a ribbon goes from the 5 inch mark to the 13 inch mark. A cord goes from the 0 mark to the 9 inch mark. Which sentence is true?
choices: The ribbon is 1 inch longer than the cord.
The cord is 1 inch longer than the ribbon.
The ribbon is 4 inches longer than the cord.
The cord is 4 inches longer than the ribbon.
questions.answer: The cord is 1 inch longer than the ribbon.
questions.solution: The ribbon is $13 - 5 = 8$ inches long. The cord starts at 0 and ends at 9, so it is 9 inches long. The cord is $9 - 8 = 1$ inch longer.

solve.answer: The cord is 1 inch longer than the ribbon.
solve.work: Ribbon: 13 - 5 = 8 in. Cord: 9 - 0 = 9 in. Cord is 1 inch longer.

questions.stem: Which sentence uses a sensible unit?
choices: A pencil is about 7 yards long.
A bus is about 12 centimeters long.
A pencil is about 7 inches long.
A ruler is about 30 meters long.
questions.answer: A pencil is about 7 inches long.
questions.solution: A pencil is short, so inches fit. A pencil is not 7 yards long. A bus is far longer than 12 centimeters, and a ruler is far shorter than 30 meters.

solve.answer: A pencil is about 7 inches long.
solve.work: A pencil is about 7 inches: sensible. A bus is not 12 cm, a pencil is not 7 yd, a ruler is not 30 m.

questions.stem: Lena's hand span is about 20 centimeters. She measures a table with her hand span and finds that the table is 5 hand spans long. About how long is the table, in centimeters?
questions.solution: Count by twenties, once for each hand span: 20, 40, 60, 80, 100. The table is about 100 centimeters long.

questions.stem: A shelf is 4 feet long. One foot is 12 inches. How long is the shelf, in inches?
questions.solution: The shelf is 4 feet, and each foot is 12 inches. Add 12 four times: $12 + 12 + 12 + 12 = 48$ inches.

questions.stem: Dan measures the same rope in feet and in yards. One yard is 3 feet. Which sentence must be true?
choices: The number of yards is bigger than the number of feet.
The two numbers are the same.
The number of feet is 3 less than the number of yards.
The number of feet is bigger than the number of yards.
questions.answer: The number of feet is bigger than the number of yards.
questions.solution: A foot is a shorter unit than a yard, so it takes more feet than yards to measure the same rope. For example, a rope that is 2 yards long is 6 feet long.

solve.answer: The number of feet is bigger than the number of yards.
solve.work: A yard is the bigger unit (3 ft), so it takes more feet than yards for the same rope; feet number = 3 times yards number.

questions.skill: Compare lengths and find the difference
questions.stem: One foot is 12 inches and one yard is 36 inches. Which length is the longest?
questions.solution: Change everything to inches. 2 feet is 24 inches. 30 inches is 30 inches. 1 yard is 36 inches. The longest is 50 inches.

solve.work: 30 in; 2 ft = 24 in; 50 in; 1 yd = 36 in. Longest: 50 inches.

questions.stem: A plant was 28 centimeters tall. It grew 15 centimeters in May and 12 centimeters in June. How tall is the plant now, in centimeters?
questions.solution: Add the starting height and the two amounts it grew: $28 + 15 = 43$, and then $43 + 12 = 55$ centimeters.

questions.stem: A ribbon is 90 centimeters long. Lia cuts off 35 centimeters for a bow and then 28 centimeters for a gift. How many centimeters of ribbon are left?
questions.solution: She cuts off $35 + 28 = 63$ centimeters in all. What is left is $90 - 63 = 27$ centimeters.

questions.stem: Mia puts toy blocks end to end along a shelf that is 40 centimeters long, with no gaps and no overlap. Each block is 5 centimeters long. How many blocks does she use to cover the whole length of the shelf?
questions.solution: Count by fives until you reach 40: 5, 10, 15, 20, 25, 30, 35, 40. That is 8 counts, so she uses 8 blocks.

solve.work: Skip count by 5 to 40: 5, 10, 15, 20, 25, 30, 35, 40 is 8 blocks.

questions.skill: Measure length with a ruler or tape
questions.stem: A strip of tape is laid along a measuring tape in centimeters. One end is at the 38 mark and the other end is at the 71 mark. How long is the strip, in centimeters?

questions.skill: Measure length with a ruler or tape
questions.stem: On a ruler in inches, a belt goes from the 6 inch mark to the 15 inch mark. A rope goes from the 0 mark to the 8 inch mark. Which statement is true?
choices: The belt is 1 inch longer than the rope
The rope is 1 inch longer than the belt
The belt is 7 inches longer than the rope
The rope is 7 inches longer than the belt
questions.answer: The belt is 1 inch longer than the rope
questions.solution: The belt is 15 - 6 = 9 inches. The rope is 8 inches. The belt is 1 inch longer.

solve.answer: The belt is 1 inch longer than the rope

questions.skill: Measure length with a ruler or tape
questions.stem: A worm is lined up with a ruler in centimeters. Its tail is at the 7 mark. Its head is 11 centimeters farther along the ruler than its tail. Which mark is the head at?
questions.solution: 7 + 11 = 18, so the head is at the 18 mark.

questions.stem: Mia puts toy blocks end to end along a ledge that is 36 centimeters long, with no gaps and no overlap. Each block is 4 centimeters long. How many blocks does she use to cover the whole ledge?
questions.solution: 4 x 9 = 36, so she uses 9 blocks.

questions.stem: Eli measures a table with a pencil. He lays it down 5 times end to end and then there is 3 centimeters left over. The pencil is 15 centimeters long. How long is the table, in centimeters?
questions.solution: 5 pencils are 5 x 15 = 75 centimeters. Add the 3 left over: 78.

questions.stem: Uma and Vic each measure the width of the same wall, one with short craft sticks and one with long boards. Vic uses the long boards. Which statement must be true?
choices: Vic counts fewer units than Uma, because his units are shorter
Vic counts fewer units than Uma, because his units are longer
Vic counts more units than Uma, because his units are longer
Vic and Uma count the same number of units
questions.answer: Vic counts fewer units than Uma, because his units are longer
questions.solution: A longer unit fits fewer times along the same wall.

solve.answer: Vic counts fewer units than Uma, because his units are longer
solve.work: Longer unit, fewer units for the same length.

questions.stem: Pick the sentence in which the unit of length makes sense.
choices: A pen is about 14 meters long.
A car is about 4 centimeters long.
A pen is about 14 centimeters long.
A hallway is about 30 inches long.
questions.answer: A pen is about 14 centimeters long.
questions.solution: A pen is small, so centimeters fit. The others use units that are too big or too small.

solve.answer: A pen is about 14 centimeters long.
solve.work: Pen 14 cm is reasonable; the others are not.

questions.stem: Which object is best measured in yards?
choices: The length of a football field
questions.answer: The length of a football field
questions.solution: Yards are a big unit, good for a field. The others are small.

solve.answer: The length of a football field
solve.work: A football field is 100 yards; others are small.

questions.stem: Ivy says her pencil is 7 meters long and her room is 4 centimeters long. What should she fix?
choices: Use centimeters for the pencil and meters for the room
Use meters for both the pencil and the room
Use centimeters for both the pencil and the room
Nothing, both lengths are fine as they are
questions.answer: Use centimeters for the pencil and meters for the room
questions.solution: A pencil is short, so centimeters fit. A room is long, so meters fit.

solve.answer: Use centimeters for the pencil and meters for the room
solve.work: Pencil about 7 cm, room about 4 m.

questions.stem: Zed measures the same table in inches and in feet. One foot is 12 inches. Which sentence must be true?
choices: The number of feet is bigger than the number of inches
The number of inches is bigger than the number of feet
The two numbers are the same
The number of inches is 12 less than the number of feet
questions.answer: The number of inches is bigger than the number of feet
questions.solution: An inch is shorter than a foot, so it takes more inches to cover the table.

solve.answer: The number of inches is bigger than the number of feet
solve.work: Inch is the shorter unit, so more of them.

questions.stem: A board is 3 feet long. One foot is 12 inches. How long is the board, in inches?
A pole is 6 feet long. One yard is 3 feet. How many yards long is the pole?
questions.solution: 3 feet make a yard. 6 feet is 3 + 3, which is 2 yards.

questions.stem: Beth's ribbon is 2 meters long. Cal's ribbon is 150 centimeters long. One meter is 100 centimeters. Whose ribbon is longer?
questions.solution: Beth's ribbon is 200 centimeters. Cal's is 150 centimeters. 200 is more.

questions.stem: Lena's hand span is about 20 centimeters. She measures a bench with her hand span and counts 6. About how long is the bench?
questions.solution: 6 hand spans of 20 centimeters: 20 x 6 = 120 centimeters.

questions.stem: Ravi's step is about 50 centimeters long. He takes 8 steps to cross a hall. About how many centimeters wide is the hall?
questions.solution: 8 steps of about 50 centimeters: 50 x 8 = 400.

questions.stem: Ola's foot is about 20 centimeters long. She walks heel to toe along a mat and counts 9 foot lengths. About how many centimeters long is the mat?
questions.solution: 9 feet of 20 centimeters: 20 x 9 = 180.

questions.skill: Compare lengths and find the difference
questions.stem: Tim's rope is 3 feet longer than Una's rope. Una's rope is 17 feet long. How many feet long is Tim's rope?

questions.skill: Compare lengths and find the difference
questions.stem: One foot is 12 inches and one yard is 36 inches. Which length is the shortest?
questions.solution: 2 feet is 24 inches and 1 yard is 36 inches. 20 inches is the shortest of 20, 24, 36 and 50.

questions.skill: Compare lengths and find the difference
questions.stem: A rope is 85 centimeters long. A string is 47 centimeters long and a ribbon is 29 centimeters long. The string and the ribbon are put end to end. How many centimeters longer is the rope than the string and ribbon together?
questions.solution: The string and ribbon together are 47 + 29 = 76 centimeters. 85 - 76 = 9.

questions.skill: Measure with a ruler or meter stick
questions.stem: Four paper strips are lined up with a ruler in inches. Strip A goes from the 8 mark to the 17 mark. Strip B goes from the 0 mark to the 12 mark. Strip C goes from the 5 mark to the 15 mark. Strip D goes from the 6 mark to the 14 mark. Which strip is the longest?
questions.solution: Subtract the start mark from the end mark. Strip A is $17 - 8 = 9$ inches. Strip B is $12 - 0 = 12$ inches. Strip C is $15 - 5 = 10$ inches. Strip D is $14 - 6 = 8$ inches. Strip B is the longest, even though it ends at the smallest mark.

questions.stem: Uma measures a table by laying pencils along it, one after another. The pencils cover the table from one end to the other, but each pencil overlaps the next one a little. She counts 6 pencils. Which statement is true about the table?
choices: The table is exactly 6 pencil lengths long, since 6 pencils were laid along it
The table is longer than 6 pencil lengths, since the overlaps add extra length
The table is about 3 pencil lengths long, since each pencil overlaps half of the next
The table is shorter than 6 pencil lengths, since parts are covered twice
questions.answer: The table is shorter than 6 pencil lengths, since parts are covered twice
questions.solution: Where two pencils overlap, that part of the table is covered twice. So the 6 pencils together are longer than the table. The table is shorter than 6 pencil lengths.

solve.answer: The table is shorter than 6 pencil lengths, since parts are covered twice
solve.work: Overlapping pencils cover some length twice, so the table is shorter than 6 full pencil lengths.

questions.stem: A rope is 5 yards long. A second rope is 13 feet long. One yard is 3 feet. How many feet longer is the first rope than the second rope?
questions.solution: Change the first rope to feet: $5 \times 3 = 15$ feet. The second rope is 13 feet. $15 - 13 = 2$, so the first rope is 2 feet longer.

questions.skill: Estimate lengths and choose a unit
questions.stem: Ana's front door is about 2 meters tall. A tree is about as tall as 4 of her doors stacked one on top of another. A tower is 5 meters taller than the tree. About how many meters tall is the tower?
questions.solution: The tree is about 4 doors tall, so it is about $4 \times 2 = 8$ meters. The tower is 5 meters taller: $8 + 5 = 13$ meters.

solve.work: Tree about 4 x 2 = 8 m (2+2+2+2). Tower 8+5 = 13 m.

questions.skill: Reading minutes from the minute hand (counting by 5s)
questions.stem: On a clock, the minute hand points to the 3. How many minutes after the hour is it?
questions.solution: Count by 5s for each number from the 12: 5, 10, 15. The minute hand on the 3 means 15 minutes after the hour.

solve.work: Each number is 5 minutes; 3 x 5 = 15 minutes after the hour.

questions.skill: Telling time to 5 minutes from the hands
questions.stem: The hour hand points to the 4. The minute hand points to the 12. What time is it?
questions.solution: The minute hand on the 12 means 0 minutes after the hour. The hour hand is on the 4, so it is 4 o'clock, which is written 4:00.

solve.work: Minute hand at 12 means :00; hour hand at 4 means 4 o'clock: 4:00.

questions.skill: Reading a digital time in words
questions.stem: A digital clock shows 7:30. Which is the same time?
questions.solution: The 7 is the hour and the 30 is the number of minutes. 7:30 is 30 minutes after 7.

questions.stem: Which digital time is 15 minutes after 9?
questions.solution: The hour is 9 and the minutes are 15, so the time is written 9:15.

questions.stem: Mia eats breakfast. Which time makes the most sense?
questions.solution: Breakfast is in the morning. Times in the morning are a.m. So 7:30 a.m. makes sense. The others are in the evening or the middle of the night.

solve.work: Breakfast is in the morning; 7:30 a.m. is morning. 2:00 a.m. is the middle of the night; p.m. times are evening/night.

questions.skill: Reading minutes from the minute hand (counting by 5s)
questions.stem: Tia says that when the minute hand points to the 10, it is 10 minutes after the hour. How many minutes after the hour is it really?
questions.solution: Each number on the clock is 5 minutes. Count by 5s ten times: 5, 10, 15, 20, 25, 30, 35, 40, 45, 50. It is 50 minutes after the hour.

solve.work: Minute hand at 10 means 10 x 5 = 50 minutes after the hour.

questions.skill: Reading a digital time in words
questions.stem: A digital clock shows 6:42. How many minutes after 6 o'clock is it?
questions.solution: The numbers after the colon tell the minutes. 6:42 is 42 minutes after 6 o'clock.

questions.skill: Telling time to 5 minutes from the hands
questions.stem: The hour hand is just past the 9. The minute hand points to the 3. What time is it?
questions.solution: The hour is 9. The minute hand on the 3 means 15 minutes (5, 10, 15). The time is 9:15. Reading the 3 as 3 minutes would give the mistake 9:03.

solve.work: Minute hand at 3 = 15 minutes; hour hand just past 9 = 9 o'clock hour: 9:15.

questions.stem: Which time is in the afternoon?
questions.solution: Times from noon until midnight are p.m. The afternoon is p.m., so 3:00 p.m. is in the afternoon. 3:00 a.m. is in the night, 9:00 a.m. is in the morning, and 11:00 p.m. is late at night.

solve.work: Afternoon is p.m. after noon and before evening. 3:00 p.m. is afternoon; 11:00 p.m. is night; a.m. times are morning/night.

questions.stem: A digital clock shows half past 4. What number is shown after the colon?
questions.solution: Half past 4 is 30 minutes after 4, so the clock shows 4:30. The number after the colon is 30.

solve.work: Half past 4 is 4:30; after the colon is 30.

questions.skill: Reading minutes from the minute hand (counting by 5s)
questions.stem: The minute hand points to the 8. How many minutes after the hour is it?
questions.solution: Count by 5s for each number: 5, 10, 15, 20, 25, 30, 35, 40. The 8 is 40 minutes.

solve.work: Each number on the clock is 5 minutes; 8 x 5 = 40.

questions.skill: Reading minutes from the minute hand (counting by 5s)
questions.stem: The minute hand points to the 6. How many minutes after the hour is that?
questions.solution: Count by 5s six times: 5, 10, 15, 20, 25, 30. The 6 means 30 minutes.

questions.skill: Reading minutes from the minute hand (counting by 5s)
questions.stem: Lila counts by 5s on a clock as the minute hand goes round. The minute hand is at the 4. What is the last number she says?
questions.solution: Counting by 5s: 5, 10, 15, 20. The 4 is 20 minutes.

solve.work: Counting by 5s from the 1 to the 4: 5, 10, 15, 20. Last number is 20.

questions.skill: Reading minutes from the minute hand (counting by 5s)
questions.stem: It is 25 minutes after the hour. Which number does the minute hand point to?
questions.solution: Each number is 5 minutes. 25 minutes is 5 fives, so the minute hand points to the 5.

solve.work: 25 / 5 = 5, so the minute hand points to the 5.

questions.skill: Telling time to 5 minutes from the hands
questions.stem: The hour hand is between the 10 and the 11. The minute hand points to the 6. What time is it?
questions.solution: The hour hand has not reached the 11, so the hour is 10. The minute hand at the 6 is 30 minutes. The time is 10:30.

solve.work: Hour hand between 10 and 11 means it is after 10; minute hand on 6 = 30 minutes. 10:30.

questions.skill: Telling time to 5 minutes from the hands
questions.stem: It is 8 o'clock. The hour hand points to the 8. Which number does the minute hand point to?
questions.solution: On the hour, the minute hand points to the 12.

solve.work: On the hour the minute hand points to the 12.

questions.skill: Telling time to 5 minutes from the hands
questions.stem: The hour hand is between the 2 and the 3, close to the 3. The minute hand points to the 9. What time is it?
questions.solution: The hour hand is almost at the 3 but has not reached it, so the hour is 2. The 9 is 45 minutes. The time is 2:45.

solve.work: Hour hand between 2 and 3, close to 3: after 2, late in the hour. Minute hand on 9 = 45 minutes. 2:45.

questions.skill: Telling time to 5 minutes from the hands
questions.stem: The hour hand points to the 6. The minute hand points to the 12. What time is it?
questions.solution: The minute hand at the 12 means 0 minutes. The hour hand at the 6 means 6. The time is 6:00.

solve.work: Minute hand at 12 = 0 minutes; hour hand on 6. 6:00.

questions.skill: Reading a digital time in words
questions.stem: A digital clock shows 2:15. Which is the same time?
questions.solution: The number before the colon is the hour, 2. The number after is the minutes, 15. So it is 15 minutes after 2.

questions.skill: Reading a digital time in words
questions.stem: A digital clock shows 9:20. How many minutes after 9 o'clock is it?
questions.solution: The 20 after the colon is the minutes. It is 20 minutes after 9 o'clock.

questions.skill: Reading a digital time in words
questions.stem: Nell's digital clock shows 11:05. How many minutes after 11 o'clock is it?
questions.solution: The number after the colon is 05, which is 5 minutes.

questions.stem: Which digital time is 45 minutes after 1 o'clock?
questions.solution: The hour is 1 and the minutes are 45. The digital time is 1:45.

questions.stem: Which digital time is half past 6?
questions.solution: Half past means 30 minutes after. Half past 6 is 6:30.

questions.stem: Jin writes 25 minutes after 3 o'clock as 3:? on a digital clock. What number is the ?
questions.solution: 25 minutes after 3 is written 3:25. The ? is 25.

questions.stem: Ivy eats lunch. Which time makes the most sense?
questions.solution: Lunch is in the middle of the day, after noon. That is p.m. 12:30 p.m. fits.

solve.work: Lunch is around midday: 12:30 p.m. (12:30 a.m. is just after midnight).

questions.stem: Sam goes to bed at night. Which time makes the most sense?
questions.solution: Bedtime is at night, which is p.m. So 9:00 p.m. fits.

questions.stem: Which time is in the morning?
questions.solution: Times with a.m. are in the morning, after midnight and before noon. 10:00 a.m. is in the morning.

questions.stem: The family eats dinner. Which time makes the most sense?
questions.solution: Dinner is in the evening, which is p.m. So 6:00 p.m. fits.

questions.stem: Which time comes first in a day, starting at midnight?
questions.solution: A day starts at midnight and goes through the a.m. hours first. 6:00 a.m. comes before every p.m. time.

solve.work: From midnight, a.m. times come before p.m. times; 6:00 a.m. is the only a.m. one.

questions.skill: Minutes before and after the hour
questions.stem: How many minutes are in 1 hour?
questions.solution: The minute hand goes all the way round in 1 hour. That is 60 minutes.

questions.skill: Minutes before and after the hour
questions.stem: Which time is exactly on the hour?
questions.solution: On the hour means 0 minutes after the hour. 8:00 has 00 minutes.

questions.skill: Minutes before and after the hour
questions.stem: The minute hand points to the 12. Which time can it be?
questions.solution: When the minute hand points to the 12, it is 0 minutes after the hour. Only 7:00 has 00 minutes.

questions.skill: Reading minutes from the minute hand (counting by 5s)
questions.stem: Ana's clock says 6:30. The minute hand points to which number?
questions.solution: The minutes are 30. Count by 5s: 5, 10, 15, 20, 25, 30. That is 6 fives, so the 6.

solve.work: 30 minutes = 6 x 5, so the minute hand points to the 6.

questions.stem: The minute hand points 3 small marks past the 6. How many minutes after the hour is it?
questions.solution: The 6 is 30 minutes (count by 5s: 5, 10, 15, 20, 25, 30). Then 3 more small marks is 3 more minutes. 30 + 3 = 33 minutes.

solve.work: 6 means 30 minutes; 3 small marks more is 33.

questions.stem: The hour hand is between the 2 and the 3, close to the 3. The minute hand points 4 small marks past the 9. What time is it?
questions.solution: The hour hand has not reached the 3, so the hour is 2. The 9 is 45 minutes, and 4 more small marks is 49 minutes. The time is 2:49.

solve.work: 9 means 45 minutes, plus 4 marks = 49. Hour hand between 2 and 3 (close to 3) means the hour is 2: 2:49.

questions.skill: Telling time to 5 minutes from the hands
questions.stem: At which time does the minute hand point to the 5?
questions.solution: The minute hand on the 5 is 25 minutes after the hour (count by 5s: 5, 10, 15, 20, 25). So the time is 2:25. At 2:05 it points to the 1, at 5:00 to the 12, and at 5:10 to the 2.

solve.work: Minute hand at 5 means 25 minutes. 2:05 -> 1, 2:25 -> 5, 5:00 -> 12, 5:10 -> 2. Answer 2:25.

questions.stem: Which digital time is the same as 20 minutes after 8?
questions.solution: The hour is 8 and the minutes are 20, so the time is 8:20. The time 7:40 is 20 minutes before 8, not after.

questions.skill: Reading a digital time in words
questions.stem: A digital clock shows 3:52. How many more minutes until it shows 4:00?
questions.solution: From 3:52 to 3:55 is 3 minutes. From 3:55 to 4:00 is 5 more minutes. 3 + 5 = 8 minutes.

questions.stem: Max gets up for school. Which time makes the most sense?
questions.solution: Max gets up in the morning, and morning times are a.m. So 7:00 a.m. makes sense. The other times are in the evening or the middle of the night.

solve.work: Getting up for school is in the morning: 7:00 a.m.

questions.solution: At 4:55 it is almost 5 o'clock, so the hour hand is almost at the 5.

No, 9:30 a.m. is in the morning and 9:30 p.m. is at night

No, both of them are at night

questions.stem: Tomas gets out of school at 3:20 in the afternoon. How is that time written?
questions.solution: The afternoon is p.m. The hour is 3 and the minutes are 20, so the time is 3:20 p.m.

questions.skill: Where the hour hand is between hours
questions.stem: Rosa and her brother look at a clock. The hour hand is between the 3 and the 4, closer to the 3. The minute hand points to the 4. Rosa says the time is 3:20. Her brother says it is 4:20. Who is right?
choices: Rosa, because the hour hand has not reached the 4 yet
Her brother, because the hour hand is past the 3
Her brother, because the minute hand points to the 4
questions.answer: Rosa, because the hour hand has not reached the 4 yet
questions.solution: The minute hand on the 4 means 20 minutes after the hour. The hour hand has not reached the 4, so the hour is 3. The time is 3:20, and Rosa is right.

solve.answer: Rosa, because the hour hand has not reached the 4 yet
solve.work: Minute hand at 4 = 20 minutes. Hour hand between 3 and 4, closer to 3, so the hour is 3: 3:20. Rosa is right because the hour hand has not reached 4. (At 3:20 the hour hand is a third of the way from 3 to 4, consistent.)

questions.stem: It is 5:48. The minute hand points 3 small marks after a number on the clock. Which number?
questions.solution: 48 minutes is 45 minutes plus 3 more. 45 minutes is 9 fives, so the minute hand is on the 9. Then 3 small marks more is 48.

solve.work: 48 = 45 + 3; 45 minutes is the 9, so 3 small marks after the 9.

questions.stem: Which digital time means a quarter past 11?

solve.work: A quarter past 11 is 15 minutes after 11: 11:15.

questions.stem: It is 10 minutes before 5 o'clock. How many minutes after 4 o'clock is it?

solve.work: 10 minutes before 5:00 is 4:50, which is 50 minutes after 4.

questions.stem: In one day, starting at midnight, which time is the latest?
questions.solution: All a.m. times come before all p.m. times. The times 9:45 a.m. and 11:50 a.m. are before noon. The time 12:05 a.m. is just after midnight, at the very start of the day. The time 12:10 p.m. is just after noon, so it is later than all the others and is the latest.

solve.work: From midnight: 12:05 a.m. (just after midnight), 9:45 a.m., 11:50 a.m., 12:10 p.m. (just after noon). Latest is 12:10 p.m.

questions.solution: 2 quarters are 50 cents. 50 + 10 + 5 = 65. The other sets make 61, 60 and 70 cents.

questions.stem: Use pennies, nickels, dimes and quarters. What is the fewest number of coins that make exactly 41 cents?
questions.solution: Start with the biggest coin that fits: a quarter (25). 16 cents are left: a dime (10), leaving 6. Then a nickel (5), leaving 1: a penny. That is 4 coins: 25 + 10 + 5 + 1 = 41. Three coins cannot make 41 cents.

solve.work: 41 = 25 + 10 + 5 + 1, 4 coins. 41 is not a multiple of 5, so at least 1 penny is needed. With 3 coins: 1 penny + 2 coins making 40 is impossible (two of 5, 10, 25 give 10, 15, 20, 30, 35, 50); 2 pennies + 1 coin making 39 is impossible. So fewest is 4.

questions.stem: Which set uses the fewest coins to make exactly 60 cents?
questions.solution: Every set is worth 60 cents. 2 quarters and 1 dime is 3 coins. The others use 5, 6 and 7 coins.

solve.work: All make 60: 1Q+3D+1N = 5 coins; 2Q+1D = 3 coins; 5D+2N = 7 coins; 6D = 6 coins. Fewest: 2 quarters and 1 dime.

questions.stem: Mia trades 3 quarters for 1 nickel and some dimes. The coins she gets are worth the same as the 3 quarters. How many dimes does she get?
questions.solution: 3 quarters are 75 cents. The nickel is 5 cents, so the dimes are worth 75 - 5 = 70 cents. 70 cents is 7 dimes.

solve.work: 3 quarters = 75 cents; minus the nickel 5 = 70 cents = 7 dimes.

questions.stem: Which set of coins makes exactly 1 dollar?
questions.solution: 1 dollar is 100 cents. 3 quarters are 75, 2 dimes are 20 and 1 nickel is 5: 75 + 20 + 5 = 100. The other sets make 105, 95 and 90 cents.

questions.stem: Tess has 1 quarter, 3 dimes and 2 nickels. How many more cents does she need to make 1 dollar?
Which pair of sets is worth the same amount of money?
questions.solution: 6 nickels are 30 cents and 3 dimes are 30 cents. The other pairs are 50 and 40, 10 and 5, and 75 and 70 cents.

solve.issues: Options like "6 nickels and 3 dimes" read naturally as one set; it works only as "6 nickels / 3 dimes". Minor wording, answer still unique.
solve.work: 10 vs 5; 50 vs 40; 30 vs 30; 75 vs 70. 6 nickels and 3 dimes match.

questions.stem: Cam has 8 dimes. Pia has 3 quarters. How many more cents does Cam have than Pia?
questions.solution: Cam has 80 cents. Pia has 75 cents. 80 - 75 = 5 cents.

questions.stem: Ora has 3 dimes and 9 nickels. How many cents does Ora have?
questions.solution: 3 dimes are 30 cents. 9 nickels are 45 cents. 30 + 45 = 75 cents.

questions.solution: 75 + 10 = 85 cents. The other sets are worth 80, 90 and 86 cents.

questions.skill: Choose coins that make an amount

questions.solution: 2 quarters and 2 dimes are 50 + 20 = 70 cents. 72 - 70 = 2 pennies.

questions.skill: Choose coins that make an amount
questions.stem: Which set of coins can NOT be used to make exactly 45 cents?
questions.solution: 25 + 10 + 1 = 36 cents, not 45. The other sets are each worth 45 cents.

solve.work: 40+5 = 45; 25+10+1 = 36; 25+10+10 = 45; 30+10+5 = 45. Only the quarter, dime, penny set cannot.

questions.skill: Choose coins that make an amount
questions.stem: Rob has 3 dimes and 2 nickels. He needs 60 cents for a toy. How many more cents does he need?
questions.solution: Rob has 30 + 10 = 40 cents. 60 - 40 = 20 cents more.

questions.stem: Use pennies, nickels, dimes and quarters. What is the fewest number of coins that make exactly 90 cents?
questions.solution: Use 3 quarters (75 cents), then 1 dime (85) and 1 nickel (90). That is 3 + 1 + 1 = 5 coins.

solve.work: 90 = 3 quarters (75) + 1 dime + 1 nickel = 5 coins; 2 quarters + 4 dimes = 6. Fewest 5.

questions.stem: Which set uses the fewest coins to make exactly 35 cents?
questions.solution: 1 quarter and 1 dime is 2 coins. The others use 4, 7 and 11 coins.

solve.work: 11 coins; 7 coins; 2 coins; 4 coins. Quarter and dime.

questions.stem: Use pennies, nickels, dimes and quarters. What is the fewest number of coins that make exactly 99 cents?

solve.work: 99 = 3 quarters + 2 dimes + 4 pennies = 9 coins (greedy is optimal for US coins).

questions.stem: Tim trades 2 quarters for 3 dimes and some nickels. The coins are worth the same. How many nickels does he get?

solve.work: 25 vs 21; 20 vs 16; 15 vs 15; 15 vs 11. 3 nickels for dime and nickel.

questions.solution: 40 + 35 = 75 cents together. 100 - 75 = 25 cents more.

solve.work: Group 1 all red, Group 2 all blue; each group has a ball, cup and hat. Sorted by color.

questions.stem: A box has these shapes: red circle, red square, blue circle, red circle, blue square, red circle. How many of them are red circles?

solve.work: red circle (1), red square, blue circle, red circle (2), blue square, red circle (3): 3 red circles.

questions.stem: Box A has 12 blocks. Box B has 9 blocks. Box C has 12 blocks. Which sentence is true?
choices: Box B has more blocks than Box A.
Box A has fewer blocks than Box C.
Box B has the same number as Box C.
Box A has more blocks than Box B.

solve.work: All three have only straight sides; triangle has 3 corners so not "4 corners".

questions.skill: Find a missing group or the total
questions.stem: Ana has 7 red beads and 3 blue beads. She puts them in 2 groups by color. How many beads does she have in all?
questions.solution: 7 + 3 = 10 beads.

questions.skill: Choose a way to sort and count the groups
questions.stem: Sort these numbers by the digit in the ones place: 12, 22, 32, 15, 25. How many groups are there?
questions.solution: The ones digits are 2 and 5. That makes 2 groups: 12, 22 and 32 in one, and 15 and 25 in the other.

questions.skill: Sort by one attribute and count
questions.stem: Ben sorts these snacks by kind: pretzel, pretzel, grape, pretzel, grape, grape, pretzel, cracker, pretzel, grape. Which kind of snack has the most?
choices: no kind; they all have the same number
questions.solution: There are 5 pretzels, 4 grapes and 1 cracker. Pretzels are the most.

questions.skill: Sort objects by one attribute and count a group
questions.stem: Ali sorts blocks by size. The blocks are: big, small, small, big, small, small, small, big. How many blocks are small?
questions.solution: Count the blocks that are small: small, small, small, small, small. That is 5 small blocks. The other 3 blocks are big.

solve.work: List: big, small, small, big, small, small, small, big. Small at positions 2,3,5,6,7 = 5.

questions.skill: Sort by one attribute and count
questions.stem: A basket has these fruits: apple, pear, apple, grape, pear, apple, apple, grape, pear, apple, apple, pear. Sort the fruit by kind. How many apples are there?
questions.solution: Count each apple in the list: the 1st, 3rd, 6th, 7th, 10th and 11th. There are 6 apples.

solve.work: 1 apple, 2 pear, 3 apple, 4 grape, 5 pear, 6 apple, 7 apple, 8 grape, 9 pear, 10 apple, 11 apple, 12 pear. Apples at 1,3,6,7,10,11 = 6.

questions.skill: Sort by one attribute and count
questions.stem: Kim sorts these numbers by whether they have a 5 in the ones place: 15, 23, 35, 41, 55, 62, 75, 85. How many of the numbers have a 5 in the ones place?
questions.solution: The numbers with 5 in the ones place are 15, 35, 55, 75 and 85. The numbers 23, 41 and 62 do not. So there are 5.

questions.stem: A farmer sorts 18 pieces of fruit by kind and color: 5 red apples, 3 green apples, 4 red pears and 6 green pears. How many pieces of fruit are red?
questions.solution: Red fruit is the red apples and the red pears. 5 + 4 = 9.

solve.work: Red: 5 red apples + 4 red pears = 9. (Total 5+3+4+6 = 18 checks.)

questions.skill: Name the attribute used to sort
questions.stem: A group has these shapes: small red circle, small red square, small red triangle. Which two attributes do all three shapes have?
questions.solution: All three are small and all three are red. They have different shapes, so shape is not shared, and the circle is the only round one.

solve.work: All three are small and red; shapes differ, so not all round; none big.

questions.stem: Jo's group is animals that have wings and 2 legs. Which animal belongs in Jo's group?
questions.solution: A bird has wings and 2 legs. A bee has wings but 6 legs. A person has 2 legs but no wings. A dog has 4 legs and no wings.

solve.work: Bird: wings and 2 legs. Bee: wings but 6 legs. Dog: no wings, 4 legs. Person: 2 legs, no wings. Answer: a bird.

questions.skill: Find the object that does not belong
questions.stem: Zoe's group is small red shapes. Her group has: small red circle, small red square, small red triangle, big red star. Which shape does not belong in the group?
questions.solution: Each shape in the group must be small and red. The big red star is red but it is big, so it does not belong.

solve.work: Group is small red shapes; the big red star is not small.

questions.stem: A teacher sorts 18 marbles by color: 6 red, 5 blue and 7 green. Which sentence is true?
choices: There are more blue marbles than red marbles.
There are as many red marbles as green marbles.
There are more green marbles than red marbles.
Red is the group with the most marbles.
questions.answer: There are more green marbles than red marbles.
questions.solution: Compare the groups: green has 7, red has 6 and blue has 5. 7 is more than 6, so there are more green marbles than red. Green is the group with the most.

solve.answer: There are more green marbles than red marbles.
solve.work: 6 red, 5 blue, 7 green (total 18). Red = green? no. Green > red? 7>6 yes. Red most? no, green. Blue > red? 5<6 no.

questions.skill: Find a missing group or the total
questions.stem: A teacher has 24 stickers. She sorts them by shape: 9 stars, 7 hearts and the rest moons. How many moons are there?
questions.solution: Stars and hearts together are 9 + 7 = 16 stickers. The moons are the rest: 24 - 16 = 8.

questions.skill: Find a missing group or the total
questions.stem: Pip sorts beads into 3 groups: 8 red beads, 9 blue beads and 6 green beads. How many beads does Pip sort in all?
questions.solution: Add the three groups: 8 + 9 = 17, and 17 + 6 = 23 beads.

questions.stem: Mia has round and square buttons that are red or blue. All the buttons are the same size and weight. She wants 4 groups: red round, red square, blue round and blue square. What should she sort by?
questions.solution: Sorting by color gives 2 groups, and sorting by shape gives 2 groups. Using both color and shape gives 4 groups. Size and weight cannot make groups, because every button is the same.

solve.work: Groups red round, red square, blue round, blue square need both color and shape.

questions.skill: Sort by one attribute and count
questions.stem: Sort these numbers by whether they are even or odd: 12, 7, 9, 18, 21, 30, 14, 5. How many of the numbers are odd?
questions.solution: The odd numbers are 7, 9, 21 and 5. That is 4 numbers.

questions.skill: Sort by one attribute and count
questions.stem: Sort these shapes by their number of sides: triangle, square, hexagon, triangle, rectangle, triangle, pentagon, triangle. Which group has the most shapes?
questions.solution: There are 4 triangles (3 sides), 2 shapes with 4 sides, 1 pentagon and 1 hexagon. The 3-sided group is biggest.

questions.stem: A teacher has 20 cards sorted by color and number: 6 red 1s, 4 red 2s, 5 blue 1s and 5 blue 2s. How many of the cards have the number 1?
questions.solution: The cards with the number 1 are 6 red and 5 blue. 6 + 5 = 11.

questions.stem: A box has a small circle, a big circle, a small square, a big square and another small circle. Which way of sorting puts the shapes into exactly 4 groups?
choices: by whether the shape has corners
questions.solution: Size gives 2 groups and shape gives 2 groups. Using both size and shape gives small circles, big circles, small squares and big squares: 4 groups.

solve.work: Size and shape: small circle, big circle, small square, big square = 4 groups; the other ways give 2.

questions.skill: Name the attribute used to sort
questions.stem: Group 1: 2, 4, 6, 8, 10. Group 2: 1, 3, 5, 7, 9. How were the numbers sorted?
choices: by the digit in the tens place
by greater than 5 and less than 5
by one digit and two digits
questions.solution: Group 1 has the even numbers and Group 2 has the odd numbers.

questions.stem: A zoo sorts 25 animals: 12 mammals, 8 birds and 5 reptiles. How many fewer reptiles than mammals are there?
questions.solution: 12 - 5 = 7 fewer reptiles.

questions.stem: A teacher sorts 16 cubes by color: 7 red, 5 blue and 4 green. Which sentence is true?
choices: There are more green cubes than blue cubes.
There are fewer red cubes than blue cubes.
There are fewer green cubes than blue cubes.
There are fewer blue cubes than green cubes.
questions.answer: There are fewer green cubes than blue cubes.
questions.solution: 4 is less than 5, so there are fewer green cubes than blue cubes. The others say the opposite or compare the wrong colors.

solve.answer: There are fewer green cubes than blue cubes.

questions.skill: Find a missing group or the total
questions.stem: A bakery has 20 rolls. It has 8 plain rolls and 7 sesame rolls. The rest are raisin rolls. How many raisin rolls are there?
questions.solution: 8 + 7 = 15, and 20 - 15 = 5 raisin rolls.

questions.skill: Find the object that does not belong
questions.stem: Zed makes a group of even numbers: 12, 14, 17, 18. Which number does not belong in his group?
questions.solution: 12, 14 and 18 are even. 17 is odd.

questions.skill: Find the object that does not belong
questions.stem: Lee makes a group of shapes with 4 straight sides: square, rectangle, trapezoid, hexagon. Which shape does not belong?
questions.solution: A square, a rectangle and a trapezoid have 4 sides. A hexagon has 6 sides.

questions.skill: Sort by one attribute and count
questions.stem: A class lists its pets: dog, dog, cat, bird, dog, cat, dog, fish, dog, dog, bird, dog, cat, dog. They sort the list by kind of pet. How many of the pets are NOT dogs?
questions.solution: There are 8 dogs in the list of 14. 14 - 8 = 6 pets are not dogs.

questions.stem: A shelf has 24 books sorted by kind and size: 8 big story books, 6 small story books, 5 big math books and 5 small math books. How many of the books are story books?
questions.solution: The story books are 8 big and 6 small. 8 + 6 = 14.

questions.skill: Name the attribute used to sort
questions.stem: A pet shop sorts its animals into 4 groups: big dogs, small dogs, big cats and small cats. Which two attributes did the shop use?
questions.solution: The groups differ by big or small (size) and by dog or cat (kind of animal). Color is never named, and dogs and cats both have 4 legs.

solve.work: Big/small = size; dogs/cats = kind of animal.

questions.skill: Choose the rule that describes a group
questions.stem: Which rule describes this group: 12, 15, 18, 19?
choices: numbers with a 1 in the ones place
numbers with a 1 in the tens place
questions.answer: numbers with a 1 in the tens place
questions.solution: Every number starts with the digit 1, so each has 1 ten. Not all are even, 12 is not greater than 15, and none has a 1 in the ones place.

solve.answer: numbers with a 1 in the tens place
solve.work: 12, 15, 18, 19 all have 1 in the tens place; not all even, 12 and 15 not > 15.

questions.skill: Sort by one attribute and count
questions.stem: Kim sorts these numbers into less than 10 and 10 or more: 3, 8, 12, 5, 17, 6. How many of the numbers are less than 10?
questions.solution: The numbers less than 10 are 3, 8, 5 and 6. That is 4 numbers.

questions.skill: Choose a way to sort and count the groups
questions.stem: Ali has big and small buttons in red, blue and green, and all of them are round. He wants to make exactly 3 groups. What should he sort by?
questions.solution: There are 3 colors, so sorting by color makes 3 groups. Size makes 2 groups, shape makes 1 group, and size with color could make up to 6.

solve.work: Colors red, blue, green give exactly 3 groups; size gives 2, shape 1, size and color 6.

questions.skill: Choose a way to sort and count the groups
questions.stem: Nell has stickers that are stars or hearts. Each shape comes in red, blue, green and yellow. She sorts them by shape and color together. How many groups does she make?
questions.solution: Each of the 2 shapes has 4 colors. 4 + 4 = 8 groups.

questions.stem: Group A has 15 marbles, Group B has 8 marbles, Group C has 15 marbles and Group D has 11 marbles. Which two groups have the same number of marbles?
questions.solution: Groups A and C both have 15 marbles.

questions.stem: A teacher sorts 30 books by size: 12 big, 11 medium and the rest small. How many more big books than small books are there?
questions.solution: The small books are 30 - 12 - 11 = 7. Then 12 - 7 = 5 more big books.

questions.skill: Find a missing group or the total
questions.stem: Zan sorts 29 cards into 3 groups. Group 1 has 10 cards and Group 2 has 12 cards. How many cards are in Group 3?

questions.skill: Choose the rule that describes a group
questions.stem: Which rule describes this group: 3, 9, 11, 17?
choices: numbers with a 1 in the tens place
questions.solution: All four numbers are odd. 11 and 17 are not less than 10, and 3 and 9 have no 1 in the tens place.

questions.skill: Sort by one attribute and count
questions.stem: Sort these numbers by whether they have a 3 in the tens place: 13, 31, 35, 23, 38, 43, 53, 63. How many of the numbers have a 3 in the tens place?
questions.solution: 31, 35 and 38 have 3 tens. The others have 3 in the ones place. So 3 numbers.

questions.stem: Jin sorts 22 socks by color and size: 4 big white, 6 small white, 7 big gray and the rest small gray. How many of the socks are gray?
questions.solution: 4 + 6 = 10 socks are white, so 22 - 10 = 12 are gray. Check: 7 big gray + 5 small gray = 12.

questions.skill: Sort by one attribute and count
questions.stem: Ed sorts these numbers by whether they are greater than 20: 7, 25, 18, 30, 21, 12, 29, 20, 24, 3, 28, 19. How many of the numbers are greater than 20?
questions.solution: The numbers greater than 20 are 25, 30, 21, 29, 24 and 28. The number 20 is not greater than 20. So there are 6.

solve.work: Greater than 20: 25, 30, 21, 29, 24, 28 = 6 (20 itself is not greater; 7, 18, 12, 3, 19 are less).

questions.skill: Sort by one attribute and count
questions.stem: A class lists the pets its students have: cat, dog, cat, cat, bird, dog, bird, cat, dog, bird, cat, cat, dog, fish. They sort the list by kind of pet. Which kind of pet appears the most?
questions.solution: Count each kind: cats 6, dogs 4, birds 3 and fish 1. The largest group is cats.

solve.work: Cats at 1,3,4,8,11,12 = 6; dogs at 2,6,9,13 = 4; birds at 5,7,10 = 3; fish 1. Total 14. Most: cat.

questions.stem: A toy box has 28 toys. They are sorted by size and color: 7 big red, 5 small red, 9 big blue and 7 small blue. How many of the toys are small?
questions.solution: Small toys are the small red ones and the small blue ones. 5 + 7 = 12.

solve.work: Small: 5 small red + 7 small blue = 12. (Total 7+5+9+7 = 28 checks.)

questions.stem: Sort these numbers by two things: even or odd, and greater or less than 10. The numbers are 4, 11, 7, 16, 9, 20, 13, 6, 15, 8, 18 and 3. How many of the numbers are even and greater than 10?
questions.solution: The numbers greater than 10 are 11, 16, 20, 13, 15 and 18. Of these, the even ones are 16, 20 and 18. So there are 3.

solve.work: Even numbers: 4, 16, 20, 6, 8, 18. Of these greater than 10: 16, 20, 18 = 3. No number equals 10.

questions.stem: Sam makes a group of things that are blue and not round. Which thing belongs in his group?
questions.solution: The thing must be blue, so the red things are out. It must not be round, so the ball is out. A blue box is blue and not round.

solve.work: Blue and not round: a blue box (ball is round; red items are not blue).

questions.skill: Name the attribute used to sort
questions.stem: Tess made 3 groups. Group A: red square, blue square, green square. Group B: red circle, blue circle, green circle. Group C: red triangle, blue triangle, green triangle. How did Tess sort the shapes?
questions.solution: Each group has only one kind of shape, but each group has all three colors. So the groups are by shape. Sorting by color would put the 3 red shapes together.

solve.work: Each group has one shape in three colors: sorted by shape (color and shape would give 9 groups).

questions.skill: Name the attribute used to sort
questions.stem: Pam has these shapes: red circle, red square, blue circle, green square, green circle, blue square. Which way of sorting makes exactly 3 groups?
choices: by whether the shape has corners
questions.solution: There are 3 colors, so sorting by color gives 3 groups: red, blue and green. Sorting by shape gives 2 groups, and sorting by whether the shape has corners also gives 2. Sorting by color and shape gives 6.

solve.work: By color: red, blue, green = 3 groups. By shape: 2. By corners: 2 (same as shape). By color and shape: 6. Answer: by color.

questions.skill: Find the object that does not belong
questions.stem: Eli's group has these numbers: 16, 19, 24 and 25. He says they are all greater than 15 and less than 25. Which number does not belong?
questions.solution: The numbers must be greater than 15 and less than 25. 16, 19 and 24 fit. 25 is not less than 25, so it does not belong.

solve.work: Greater than 15 and less than 25: 16, 19, 24 fit; 25 is not less than 25.

questions.stem: A class counts 26 pets: 6 cats, 15 dogs and 5 fish. How many more dogs are there than cats and fish together?
questions.solution: Cats and fish together are 6 + 5 = 11. There are 15 dogs, and 15 - 11 = 4 more dogs.

solve.work: Cats and fish together 6+5 = 11. Dogs 15. 15-11 = 4. (Total 26 checks.)

questions.skill: Find a missing group or the total
questions.stem: A bag has 30 buttons. They are sorted by color. There are 11 red buttons. There are 2 more blue buttons than red buttons. The rest of the buttons are green. How many green buttons are there?
questions.solution: Blue buttons: 11 + 2 = 13. Red and blue together are 11 + 13 = 24. The green buttons are the rest: 30 - 24 = 6.

questions.skill: Find a missing group or the total
questions.stem: Lia sorts 30 beads by color. 9 are red, 7 are blue and 8 are green. The rest are yellow. How many beads are yellow?
questions.solution: 9 + 7 + 8 = 24, and 30 - 24 = 6 yellow beads.

questions.stem: There are 30 shapes. 12 are circles and the rest are squares. Of the circles, 7 are red. Of the squares, 9 are red. How many of the shapes are red?
questions.solution: 7 red circles + 9 red squares = 16 red shapes.

questions.stem: A table has 24 cubes sorted by size and color: 5 big red, 7 small red, 6 big blue and the rest small blue. How many more small cubes than big cubes are there?
questions.solution: Small blue = 24 - 5 - 7 - 6 = 6. Small cubes = 7 + 6 = 13. Big cubes = 5 + 6 = 11. 13 - 11 = 2.

questions.stem: Flowers are sorted by kind: 9 roses, 7 daisies and 10 tulips. How many fewer tulips than roses and daisies together are there?
questions.solution: Roses and daisies: 9 + 7 = 16. 16 - 10 = 6 fewer tulips.

questions.skill: Find a missing group or the total
questions.stem: A teacher sorts 28 pencils into 3 boxes. The first box has 9 pencils. The second box has 4 more pencils than the first box. How many pencils are in the third box?
questions.solution: The second box has 9 + 4 = 13. The first two boxes have 9 + 13 = 22. 28 - 22 = 6 pencils in the third box.

questions.skill: Find a missing group or the total
questions.stem: Sam sorts 30 cards. The red group has 8 cards. The blue group has 5 fewer cards than the red group. The green group has the rest. How many cards are in the green group?
questions.solution: Blue = 8 - 5 = 3. Red and blue = 8 + 3 = 11. Green = 30 - 11 = 19.

questions.stem: A teacher sorts 27 stickers: 8 stars, 9 hearts and 10 moons. Which sentence is true?
choices: Stars and moons together are fewer than hearts.
Stars and hearts together are more than moons.
questions.answer: Stars and hearts together are more than moons.
questions.solution: Stars and hearts: 8 + 9 = 17, which is more than 10 moons. Stars and moons are 18, not fewer than 9. 10 is not fewer than 8, and 9 is not fewer than 8.

solve.answer: Stars and hearts together are more than moons.

questions.stem: Sort numbers by two things: even or odd, and greater or less than 30. Which of these numbers is odd and greater than 30?
questions.solution: 35 is odd and greater than 30. 28 and 42 are even, and 29 is odd but less than 30.

questions.stem: A box has a big red ball, a small blue ball, a big blue block and a small red block. Max's group is things that are big and NOT red. Which thing belongs in his group?
questions.solution: The big blue block is big and is not red. The big red ball is red, and the small things are not big.

solve.work: Big and not red: big blue block.

questions.skill: Find the object that does not belong

questions.solution: 11, 19 and 23 are odd and greater than 10. 14 is even.

questions.skill: Find the object that does not belong
questions.stem: Ned makes a group of shapes that have an even number of sides: square, rectangle, hexagon, triangle. Which shape does not belong?
questions.solution: A square and a rectangle have 4 sides and a hexagon has 6, which are even. A triangle has 3 sides, which is odd.

questions.skill: Name the attribute used to sort
questions.stem: Rob sorts number cards into two groups. Group 1: 14, 24, 34, 54. Group 2: 41, 42, 43, 45. How were the numbers sorted?
choices: by whether the number is even or odd
by whether the number is greater than 40
by whether the number has one digit or two digits
by whether the 4 is in the ones place or the tens place
questions.answer: by whether the 4 is in the ones place or the tens place
questions.solution: Every number in Group 1 ends in 4. Every number in Group 2 starts with 4. Group 2 has both even and odd numbers, Group 1 has 54 which is greater than 40, and all of the numbers have two digits.

solve.answer: by whether the 4 is in the ones place or the tens place
solve.work: Group 1 has 4 in ones place, group 2 has 4 in tens place. 54 > 40 rules out the "greater than 40" rule; group 2 has odd and even.

questions.skill: Choose the rule that describes a group
questions.stem: Which rule describes this group: 12, 14, 16, 18?
questions.solution: All are even and all are between 10 and 20. 12 is not greater than 12, and 18 is not less than 18.

solve.work: 12-18 even, all between 10 and 20; 18 not < 18, 12 not > 12.

questions.skill: Choose a way to sort and count the groups
questions.stem: A teacher wants to sort 30 children into groups so that every child is in exactly one group. Which two groups work?
choices: children who ride the bus and children who walk
children who ride the bus and children who do not ride the bus
children who wear glasses and children who ride the bus
girls and children who like pizza
questions.answer: children who ride the bus and children who do not ride the bus
questions.solution: Every child either rides the bus or does not, so each is in exactly one group. Some children may take a car, so riding and walking leave some out. The last two choices overlap or leave some out.

solve.answer: children who ride the bus and children who do not ride the bus
solve.work: Bus / not bus covers every child exactly once.

questions.skill: Choose a way to sort and count the groups

questions.solution: The tens digits are 5, 2, 5, 3, 2, 5, 3, 5. The different digits are 5, 2 and 3, so there are 3 groups.

questions.skill: Sort by one attribute and count

questions.solution: 30 - 12 = 18 coins are not pennies.

questions.skill: Find a missing group or the total
questions.stem: A teacher sorts 28 children into a red team and a blue team. 15 children are on the red team. Then 4 children move from the red team to the blue team. How many children are on the blue team now?
questions.solution: At first the blue team has 28 - 15 = 13 children. After 4 move over, 13 + 4 = 17.

questions.skill: Find a missing group or the total
questions.stem: Ola sorts 24 objects into 3 groups. Which list could be the sizes of her 3 groups?
questions.solution: 10 + 8 + 6 = 24. The other lists add to 25, 26 and 23.

questions.skill: Sort by one attribute and count
questions.stem: Eli lists the colors of 16 cars: red, white, blue, white, white, red, black, white, blue, red, white, black, red, white, blue, white. He sorts the cars by color. Which color has the second most cars?
questions.solution: White has 7, red has 4, blue has 3 and black has 2. Red has the second most.

solve.work: White 7, red 4, blue 3, black 2 (total 16). Second most: red.

questions.stem: A teacher sorts 29 stickers. There are 10 stars. There are 3 more hearts than stars. The rest are moons. How many more hearts than moons are there?
questions.solution: Hearts = 10 + 3 = 13. Moons = 29 - 10 - 13 = 6. 13 - 6 = 7 more hearts.

questions.stem: Mark sorts shapes by color and shape: 3 red circles, 2 blue circles, 4 red squares and 3 blue squares. Which sentence is true?
choices: There are more squares than circles.
There are more circles than squares.
There are more blue shapes than red shapes.
There are as many red shapes as blue shapes.
questions.answer: There are more squares than circles.
questions.solution: Squares: 4 + 3 = 7. Circles: 3 + 2 = 5. Red: 7, blue: 5. So there are more squares than circles; the other sentences are false.

solve.answer: There are more squares than circles.

questions.stem: A box has 30 toys sorted by kind and color: 8 red cars, 5 blue cars, 9 red blocks and 8 blue blocks. How many of the toys are blue?
questions.solution: 5 blue cars + 8 blue blocks = 13 blue toys.

questions.skill: Name the attribute used to sort
questions.stem: Group 1: 10, 12, 14. Group 2: 20, 22, 24. Group 3: 30, 32, 34. How were the numbers sorted?
choices: by the digit in the ones place
by the digit in the tens place
by whether they are even or odd
by whether they are less than 20
questions.answer: by the digit in the tens place
questions.solution: Each group has the same tens digit: 1, 2 and 3. The ones digits repeat in every group, and every number is even.

solve.answer: by the digit in the tens place
solve.work: Groups share tens digit 1, 2, 3; all are even.

solve.work: Cats row has 3 X, each 1 pet: 3 cats.

questions.solution: The Jump rope bar reaches 6, so Jump rope got 6 votes.

questions.solution: Look for the bar that reaches 9. That is the Tuesday bar, so 9 apples were picked on Tuesday.

questions.solution: Count each row: 4 cars, 3 balls and 2 blocks. $4 + 3 + 2 = 9$ toys in all.

questions.solution: $8 - 5 = 3$, so 3 more children chose red than green.

questions.solution: Count each row: Summer 7, Winter 3, Spring 5, Fall 4. Summer has the most X marks (7).

solve.work: Summer 7, Winter 3, Spring 5, Fall 4. Most: Summer.

questions.skill: Find the most or least popular category
questions.stem: A bar graph shows the fish in a tank. The Goldfish bar reaches 6. The Guppy bar reaches 3. The Tetra bar reaches 8. The Angelfish bar reaches 5. Which kind of fish has the fewest?
questions.solution: The shortest bar is Guppy, at 3. So there are fewer guppies than any other kind.

solve.work: Goldfish 6, Guppy 3, Tetra 8, Angelfish 5. Fewest: Guppy.

solve.work: apple at positions 1, 3, 4, 6, 8 = 5; grape at 2, 5, 7 = 3; total 8.

collecting the answers from the children
drawing the bars of the graph
looking at the graph to see what it shows
questions.answer: looking at the graph to see what it shows
questions.solution: Looking at the finished graph to see what it shows is the step of analyzing the data.

solve.answer: looking at the graph to see what it shows

questions.skill: Pose a question and follow the data cycle
questions.stem: Mo wants to know the favorite drink of the 24 children in his class. Which plan is best?
choices: ask each of the 24 children and record every answer
ask only 2 of his friends and use their answers
ask his sister at home and use her answer
guess which drink the children like the most
questions.answer: ask each of the 24 children and record every answer
questions.solution: Asking everyone in the class and recording each answer shows the favorite drink of the class.

solve.answer: ask each of the 24 children and record every answer

questions.skill: Parts of a graph and spotting mistakes
questions.stem: Nia's data says Apples 8, Pears 5 and Plums 7. Her bar graph has bars reaching 8 for apples, 5 for pears and 8 for plums. What is wrong with her graph?
choices: the Apples bar is 1 too high
the Plums bar is 1 too high
the graph has one bar too many
questions.answer: the Plums bar is 1 too high
questions.solution: Plums should reach 7, but the bar reaches 8, so it is 1 too high.

solve.answer: the Plums bar is 1 too high

questions.skill: Use a graph to draw and check conclusions
questions.stem: A bar graph shows the club each child chose. Art has 7 children, Music has 9, Chess has 5 and Drama has 8. Each child chose one club. Ana says, "More than 30 children are in the clubs." Is she right?
choices: Yes, there are 31 children in all.
No, there are 28 children in all.
No, there are 29 children in all.
Yes, there are 33 children in all.
questions.answer: No, there are 29 children in all.
questions.solution: 7 + 9 + 5 + 8 = 29, which is not more than 30.

solve.answer: No, there are 29 children in all.

questions.stem: A bar graph shows where 28 children like to go. The Hike bar reaches 16. The Swim bar is 4 lower than the Hike bar. How many children chose hike and swim together?
questions.solution: Swim = 16 - 4 = 12. Hike and swim together = 16 + 12 = 28.

questions.skill: Find the most or least popular category
questions.stem: A bar graph shows votes. Red has 14, Blue has 6, Green has 8 and Yellow has 5. Which two colors together have the same number of votes as Red?
questions.solution: Blue + Green = 6 + 8 = 14, the same as Red. The other pairs total 11, 13 and 20.

questions.skill: Find how many more or fewer
questions.stem: A bar graph shows the colors 30 children chose. Red has 8, Blue has 11 and Green has 5. The rest chose Yellow. How many more children chose Blue than chose Yellow?
questions.solution: Yellow = 30 - 8 - 11 - 5 = 6. Then 11 - 6 = 5 more chose Blue.

questions.stem: Which title best fits a graph that shows how many children in Room 4 like each pet?
questions.solution: A good title says what the graph is about and whose data it shows.

questions.skill: Collect and count data (up to 30 data points)
questions.stem: Ivy writes how many pets each of 12 children has: 2, 0, 1, 3, 1, 2, 0, 1, 2, 1, 0, 4. How many of the children have at least 2 pets?
questions.solution: The children with 2 or more pets are 2, 3, 2, 2 and 4. That is 5 children.

questions.skill: Make a graph from data (rows and bars)
questions.stem: Tara has this data: Tigers 6, Lions 9, Bears 4. She makes a bar graph. Which list tells how high each bar should reach?
questions.solution: Each bar should reach its own number: Tigers 6, Lions 9, Bears 4.

questions.skill: Use a graph to draw and check conclusions
questions.stem: A bar graph shows what 29 children chose. Soccer reaches 10, Tennis reaches 4, Golf reaches 3 and Swimming reaches 12. Which conclusion does the graph show?
choices: Swimming got more votes than Soccer and Golf together.
Golf and Tennis together got more votes than Soccer.
Soccer and Tennis together got more votes than Swimming.
Tennis got fewer votes than Golf did.
questions.answer: Soccer and Tennis together got more votes than Swimming.
questions.solution: Soccer + Tennis = 14, more than 12. Soccer + Golf = 13, more than 12. Golf + Tennis = 7, less than 10. Tennis (4) got more than Golf (3).

solve.answer: Soccer and Tennis together got more votes than Swimming.

questions.skill: Collect and count data (up to 30 data points)
questions.stem: Gus writes 30 answers in a tally chart. He counts A as 11, B as 9 and C as 7, which is 27 in all. What should he do?
choices: make the graph now, since 27 is close enough
add 3 to the A tally without counting again
change the C tally to 10 without counting again
count the tally marks again, since 27 is not 30
questions.answer: count the tally marks again, since 27 is not 30
questions.solution: There should be 30 answers, but the tallies add to 11 + 9 + 7 = 27. Something was missed, so he should count again.

solve.answer: count the tally marks again, since 27 is not 30

questions.skill: Find the most or least popular category
questions.stem: A bar graph shows what 30 children chose. A reaches 13, B reaches 8, C reaches 6 and D reaches 3. How many fewer children chose the most popular category than chose the other three categories together?
questions.solution: The other three: 8 + 6 + 3 = 17. 17 - 13 = 4 fewer.

questions.skill: Use a graph to draw and check conclusions
questions.stem: A bar graph shows what 30 children said. The Yes bar reaches 17. The No bar reaches 13. Which sentence is true?
choices: More than half of the 30 children said yes.
Exactly half of the 30 children said yes.
More than half of the 30 children said no.
Fewer than 10 of the 30 children said no.
questions.answer: More than half of the 30 children said yes.
questions.solution: Half of 30 is 15. 17 is more than 15, so more than half said yes.

solve.answer: More than half of the 30 children said yes.
